evidence: Caes. B.G. 2.11: magnō cum strepitū ac tumultū
terms.comment: Any loud, confused noise: of wheels, doors, rivers, a crowd, the city (Lewis & Short). To make a noise is strepere (see noisy).
A sound of any kind, of hooves, oars, wind or thunder, not necessarily unpleasant; strepitus is noise as din.
A shout or outcry, and the noise of many voices together.

terms.gloss: a rattle, a clatter, a creak
terms.comment: A sharp, short noise: the flapping of wings, the creak of a door, the crackle of fire.

phrases.latin: tantō silentiō in summum ēvāsēre ut nōn custōdēs sōlum fallerent, sed nē canēs quidem, sollicitum animal ad nocturnōs strepitūs, excitārent
phrases.english: they reached the top so quietly that they not only slipped past the guards but did not even wake the dogs, creatures that fret at every noise in the night

phrases.latin: ecce undique mē varius clāmor circumsonat: suprā ipsum balneum habitō
phrases.english: listen: noise of every kind surrounds me; I live right above a bath-house
